name: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
venue: ICLR 2024 (The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations; accepted as Oral, top 1%). OpenReview id hSyW5go0v8 / DBLP conf/iclr/AsaiWWSH24. Preprint arXiv:2310.11511 (submitted 17 Oct 2023).
authors_affiliation: Akari Asai (University of Washington / Allen Institute for AI; lead author, IBM Fellowship), Zeqiu Wu (University of Washington), Yizhong Wang (University of Washington), Avirup Sil (IBM Research AI), Hannaneh Hajishirzi (University of Washington / Allen Institute for AI). Primary affiliations: University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI (AI2), and IBM Research AI.
code_url: https://github.com/AkariAsai/self-rag (MIT license; ~2.4k stars). Models: HuggingFace selfrag/selfrag_llama2_7b and selfrag/selfrag_llama2_13b; training data: selfrag/selfrag_train_data (150K instances); project site https://selfrag.github.io/.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/AkariAsai/self-rag (original research repo; last substantive update Mar 2024; not a continuously-maintained leaderboard/paper-list). Community fine-tune: SciPhi/SciPhi-Self-RAG-Mistral-7B-32k.
task_domain: QA / knowledge-intensive NLG. Open-domain QA (PopQA, TriviaQA-unfiltered), closed-set tasks (fact verification PubHealth, multiple-choice reasoning ARC-Challenge), and long-form generation (biography generation / FactScore, ASQA long-form QA with citations). Not an agent/tool-use/planning setting.
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, non-interactive generation. A single arbitrary LM (Llama2-7B / 13B) is trained to interleave on-demand retrieval, generation, and self-critique by emitting special 'reflection tokens', evaluated zero-shot (no few-shot demonstrations) across six tasks. Supervision is available but synthetic: reflection-token labels are distilled offline from GPT-4 into an in-house Critic model C, which then annotates a 150K-instance instruction-following + knowledge-intensive corpus that trains the Generator M via standard next-token prediction. The retriever (Contriever-MSMARCO) is frozen off-the-shelf; only the Critic and Generator LMs are trained. At inference the model itself decides whether/when to retrieve (via a [Retrieve] token, optionally thresholded) and ranks passage-conditioned segment candidates using its own critique-token probabilities in a segment-level beam search.
what_is_retrieved: docs (text passages from a Wikipedia corpus) retrieved on-demand to provide factual grounding. No demos/cases/trajectories/skills/tools/experiences are retrieved.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (Wikipedia passages, plus Google Programmable Search intro paragraphs for some open-ended tasks). No agent-written growing/episodic memory; the corpus is fixed at test time.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k document retrieval per retrieval call (top-5 by default, top-10 for PopQA), but the operative selection is precision-driven over GENERATED SEGMENTS rather than over documents: for each retrieved passage the model generates a candidate continuation and selects/ranks via critique-token (IsRel/IsSup/IsUse) scores in a segment-level beam search. The objective is on-demand, quality-controlled use of retrieval, not recovery of a complete minimal document set and not a fixed document ranking.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A - not a case-based-reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle over a case base. [Retrieve: no (retrieves passages, not cases), Reuse: no, Revise: no, Retain: no].
explicit_cbr_grounding: false. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is framed as self-reflective retrieval-augmented generation with reflection tokens.
retrieval_unit: document/passage. Contriever-MSMARCO retrieves Wikipedia text passages (DPR-style psgs_w100 100-word chunks / 2020 preprocessed Wikipedia for PopQA). Retrieval granularity is the passage; generation is organized at the segment (sentence) level.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-built. By default the official Contriever Wikipedia embeddings over 2018 English Wikipedia; for PopQA the December 2020 preprocessed Wikipedia; bio-generation and open-domain QA additionally retrieve via Google Programmable Search (Wikipedia introductory paragraphs). Store is frozen at test time; nothing is induced online.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index (Contriever passage embeddings, nearest-neighbor / FAISS-style search). No graph or hierarchical structure.
retriever_type: Dense (off-the-shelf Contriever-MSMARCO bi-encoder, Izacard et al. 2022). Optionally augmented with the Google Programmable Search API for some open-ended tasks. The novel 'retrieve-on-demand' decision is made by the GENERATIVE LM emitting a [Retrieve] reflection token, but document scoring itself is dense retrieval.
retriever_learning_signal: none for the retriever (Contriever-MSMARCO is frozen off-the-shelf, not fine-tuned). The LM's retrieve-or-not [Retrieve] token IS learned, via supervised next-token prediction on Critic-distilled labels (Critic data distilled from GPT-4), but this trains the decision policy inside the LM, not the document retriever. The authors explicitly leave instruction-tuned/jointly-trained retrievers to future work.
query_construction: Raw input prompt plus preceding generation. The retrieval query is (x, y_{<t}): the original input x together with the previously generated segment y_{t-1}, so retrieval at a later segment is conditioned on what has already been generated. No explicit decomposition/expansion; the [Retrieve] token gates whether the query is issued.
query_granularity: Step/segment-level (interleaved). The model can retrieve at the start and again at each subsequent segment (sentence) during generation, conditioning each retrieval on x and the preceding generation; it can also skip retrieval entirely. Not a single task-level one-shot query.
when_to_retrieve: adaptive (learned, model-initiated) and on-demand: the LM emits a [Retrieve] = {yes, no, continue} reflection token to decide per segment whether to retrieve. A soft threshold on the normalized P([Retrieve]=Yes) probability can additionally tune retrieval frequency at inference. Can be forced to no_retrieval / always_retrieve / adaptive_retrieval modes.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Reflection token: the model-generated [Retrieve] token (values yes / no / continue), produced by the LM as part of decoding. Optionally a confidence threshold on the normalized probability of [Retrieve]=Yes over the retrieval-token vocabulary triggers retrieval (larger threshold -> less retrieval). This is a learned, self-reflective signal rather than a fixed schedule, token-perplexity heuristic (FLARE), or external classifier (Adaptive-RAG).
reranking: Segment-level critique-guided reranking rather than a document cross-encoder. When retrieval fires, K passages are processed in parallel to produce K candidate continuations; a segment-level beam search (default beam width B=2) ranks candidates by a critic score S = linear weighted sum of normalized desirable-critique-token probabilities (IsRel, IsSup, IsUse). No separate cross-encoder/RRF/instruction-tuned reranker over documents.
retrieved_context_refinement: Relevance/support self-evaluation and selection (a self-reflection filter): the model emits IsRel (relevant/irrelevant) to judge each passage and IsSup (fully/partially/no support) to judge whether its own segment is grounded, and can hard-filter undesirable continuations (e.g., IsRel=Irrelevant) or down-weight them softly. No decompose-recompose, summarization/compression (contrasted with Recomp), or reason-in-documents distillation; refinement is critique-token-based selection.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (retrieves plain Wikipedia passages, not tool/skill descriptions; no docstring/synthetic-query/weighted-field engineering).
index_content_separation: N/A. No lightweight-index-then-content / progressive-disclosure separation; full passages are embedded and retrieved directly.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A. Static document index; no tool API / RapidAPI / RESTful / MCP / function-calling integration (the only API is Google Programmable Search used as a retrieval source, not a live tool index).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A. No tools and no inter-tool dependency modeling.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation with self-critique: retrieved passages are inserted (wrapped in <paragraph>...</paragraph> markup) into the LM input, and the LM generates a passage-conditioned continuation plus reflection tokens (IsRel/IsSup/IsUse) that are used to score and select the output segment. Reflection tokens are also a TRAINING signal (the LM is trained to predict them as ordinary next tokens from the expanded vocabulary), making them both an inference-time controller and a learned latent-control mechanism.
planning_integration: Per-segment interleaved retrieve-generate-critique inside a segment-level beam (tree) search. At each segment step t the model decides to retrieve (or not); if retrieving, K passages are expanded in parallel into K continuations and the top-B continuations are kept by critique-weighted score, returning the best full sequence at the end. No external planner/MCTS over actions; the 'search' is over output segments conditioned on passages.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-segment (sentence-level). Retrieval, generation, and critique are interleaved at the granularity of each generated segment/sentence, not per-token, per-CoT-step, or per-tool-call.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not CBR; no retrieved case is adapted/revised). The analogue is that the LM conditions generation on retrieved passages and self-critiques via reflection tokens, but there is no case adaptation step.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved passages injected as text (delimited by <paragraph> context markup), accompanied by model-generated reflection tokens. What is injected is concrete passage text, not distilled strategies, workflows, programs, or soft/latent tokens (reflection tokens are discrete special vocabulary tokens, not the retrieved content).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw passage/document (single concrete Wikipedia passage). No distilled strategy, state-aware guideline, reusable workflow, or procedural skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Self-reflection relevance/support evaluation: the model is trained to predict and act on IsRel (passage relevance) and IsSup (whether its segment is supported by the passage), enabling it to discount irrelevant retrieved passages via soft weighting or hard filtering in the segment-level beam search. The ablation shows that naively using the top passage regardless of relevance ('Retrieve top1', as in standard RAG) causes large drops on PopQA and ASQA, evidencing the robustness benefit of critique-based selection.
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow/graph/latent memory). The only persistent learned artifacts are the trained Critic and Generator LMs and the expanded reflection-token vocabulary; the retrievable store is a fixed external Wikipedia corpus.
write_back: false. No new experiences/cases/passages are written back to any store at deployment; the retrieval corpus is static and the model weights are fixed after offline training.
online_growth: false. The retrievable corpus is frozen after offline construction; nothing grows at test time.
write_back_trigger: never. There is no memory write-back at inference; reflection-token supervision is created once offline (GPT-4 -> Critic -> annotated 150K corpus -> Generator) and then frozen.
failure_experience_usage: Not as stored retrievable experience. During offline TRAINING the Critic learns to emit negative/undesirable reflection tokens (e.g., IsRel=Irrelevant, IsSup=No support, low IsUse) so the Generator learns to recognize unsupported/irrelevant cases, but these are token-level supervision signals, not a stored failure memory retrieved at test time. At inference, undesirable critique tokens are used to filter/down-weight continuations within the current query, not stored.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored memory entries to mutate). Model weights are fixed after offline training; no online update.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partial. The WHEN-to-retrieve decision is a learned policy embedded in the LM (the [Retrieve] reflection token, trained via supervised next-token prediction on Critic-distilled labels), and segment selection is driven by learned critique-token probabilities. However, this is supervised distillation, NOT RL / value-based / M-MDP policy learning, and the document retriever itself remains a fixed off-the-shelf dense top-k.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A. Single-agent, single private model; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.
benchmarks: Six tasks: (1) PopQA (long-tail open-domain QA, accuracy/match), (2) TriviaQA-unfiltered (TQA, open-domain QA, accuracy), (3) PubHealth (Pub, public-health fact verification, accuracy), (4) ARC-Challenge (ARC, multiple-choice scientific reasoning, accuracy), (5) Biography generation / FactScore (Bio, factual precision FS), (6) ASQA (long-form QA with citations; metrics: str-em (em), rouge (rg), MAUVE (mau), citation precision (pre), citation recall (rec)).
benchmark_family: QA (open-domain single-hop: PopQA, TriviaQA) + closed-set fact verification/reasoning (PubHealth, ARC-Challenge) + long-form knowledge generation with attribution (FactScore/Bio, ASQA). Not multi-hop / web / embodied / tool / code / memory / decision-RL families.
baselines: Without retrieval: Llama2-7B/13B, Alpaca-7B/13B, CoVE-65B*, plus proprietary ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo-0301). With retrieval: Toolformer*-6B, retrieval-augmented Llama2-7B/13B and Alpaca-7B/13B, Llama2-FT-7B (same instruction-output data as Self-RAG but no retrieval/reflection in training, retrieval-augmented only at test time), SAIL*-7B, retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat-13B (Ret-Llama2-c13B), retrieval-augmented ChatGPT (Ret-ChatGPT), and Perplexity.ai. (* numbers cited from original papers.)
key_metrics: Accuracy/match (PopQA, TQA, PubHealth, ARC); FactScore (FS) for Bio; for ASQA: str-em (em), rouge (rg), MAUVE (mau, fluency), citation precision (pre) and citation recall (rec). Analyses also report retrieval frequency vs accuracy.
headline_result: Self-RAG (7B and 13B) outperforms ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat on most of the six tasks. Self-RAG-7B: PopQA 54.9, TQA 66.4, PubHealth 72.4, ARC 67.3, Bio FactScore 81.2, ASQA em 30.0 / rg 35.7 / MAUVE 74.3 / citation precision 66.9 / recall 67.8. Self-RAG-13B: PopQA 55.8, TQA 69.3, PubHealth 74.5, ARC 73.1, Bio FactScore 80.2, ASQA em 31.7 / rg 37.0 / MAUVE 71.6 / citation prec 70.3 / recall 71.3. For comparison, ChatGPT: PopQA 29.3, PubHealth 70.1, ARC 75.3, Bio 71.8; Ret-ChatGPT: PopQA 50.8, ASQA citation prec 65.1 / rec 76.6; Ret-Llama2-chat-13B: PopQA 51.8, PubHealth 52.1, Bio 79.9, ASQA citation prec 19.8 / rec 36.1. Most-cited single claim: Self-RAG substantially improves factuality (FactScore) and citation accuracy in long-form generation over ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat.
ablations: Table 3a (7B model, trained on a 50k subset; PopQA acc / PubHealth-Med acc / ASQA em). Full Self-RAG(50k): 45.5 / 73.5 / 32.1. Training ablations: No Retriever (standard instruction-tuning without retrieved passages) 43.6 / 67.8 / 31.0; No Critic (trained on input-output always augmented with top-1 retrieved doc, no reflection tokens, similar to SAIL) 42.6 / 72.0 / 18.1 - large ASQA drop. Inference ablations: No retrieval 24.7 / 73.0 / - (PopQA collapses, ~40% relative drop); Hard constraints (retrieve whenever IsRel triggers, no adaptive threshold) 28.3 / 72.6 / -; Retrieve top1 (always use top passage, standard RAG) 41.8 / 73.1 / 28.6 - large PopQA/ASQA drop; Remove IsSup (drop IsSup from beam-search score) 44.1 / 73.2 / 30.6 - hurts ASQA. Conclusion: all training and inference components matter; critique-based fine-grained selection beats naive top-passage use. Additional analyses: (b) increasing IsSup weight raises ASQA citation precision but lowers MAUVE/fluency (test-time customization); (c) raising the retrieval threshold reduces retrieval frequency with small loss on PubHealth (~2%) but large loss on PopQA (~40% relative); training-data-scale analysis (5k/10k/20k/50k vs 150k) shows upward trajectories, larger gains on PopQA/ASQA; human evaluation finds reflection-token predictions (IsRel, IsSup) mostly align with annotators (S&P PopQA 92.5 / Bio 70.0; IsRel 95.0/90.0; IsSup 90.0/85.0). Critic agreement with GPT-4 >90% (e.g., Llama2-7B critic: Retrieve 93.8, IsSup 93.5, IsRel 80.2, IsUse 73.5).
evaluation_decoupling: Partial. Self-RAG reports task-level end-to-end metrics (accuracy/FactScore/ASQA suite) and, separately, intrinsic reliability of the reflection-token predictions via Critic-vs-GPT-4 agreement (>90%) and human-vs-model agreement for IsRel/IsSup, and retrieval-frequency-vs-accuracy curves. It does not report standard retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) for the document retriever.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Outcome: task accuracy, FactScore, ASQA str-em/rouge/MAUVE/citation precision/recall. Process: reliability/agreement of predicted reflection tokens (IsRel, IsSup) against human and GPT-4 judgments, citation precision/recall as attribution-process quality, and retrieval frequency.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Adaptive retrieval is the efficiency lever: an inference-time threshold on P([Retrieve]=Yes) trades retrieval frequency for accuracy (Figure 3c) - on PubHealth retrieving less costs ~2% accuracy, on PopQA ~40% relative drop. The framework avoids RLHF (no PPO training) by inserting reflection tokens offline, described as more memory-efficient and stable than RLHF; behavior is customized at test time by adjusting critique weights without retraining. Segment-level beam search uses beam width B=2 and processes K passages in parallel (extra inference compute vs single-pass RAG). No explicit per-query latency/API-cost table is reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k retrieval per call: top-5 documents by default (Contriever-MSMARCO), top-10 for PopQA, with max_new_tokens ~100 (short-form) / 300 (long-form, max_depth T up to 6-7); segment-level beam width B=2. k is fixed, not adaptive/precision-driven at the document level; the adaptive lever is WHETHER to retrieve (the [Retrieve] token / threshold) plus critique-based segment selection rather than variable document k.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks; no new benchmark constructed). Training data: 150K instances annotated with reflection tokens, sourced from instruction-following data (GPT-4 Alpaca 26,168; Stanford Alpaca 25,153; FLAN-V2 17,817; ShareGPT 13,406; Open Assistant 1 9,464 - via Open-Instruct) and knowledge-intensive data (Wizard of Wikipedia 17,367; Natural Questions 15,535; FEVER 9,966; OpenBookQA 4,699; ARC-Easy 2,147; ASQA 3,897 - via KILT/HF/ASQA). Critic training collected via GPT-4 (e.g., ~19,317 relevance, ~11,181 utility, ~1,294 IsRel, ~3,831 utility-type instances per the appendix counts).
builds_on: Standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Lewis et al. 2020; Guu et al. 2020; Ram et al. 2023 in-context RAG); Contriever-MSMARCO dense retriever (Izacard et al. 2022); Llama2-7B/13B (Touvron et al. 2023) as base LMs; GPT-4 (OpenAI 2023) as the Critic teacher; Open-Instruct instruction-tuning data and KILT knowledge-intensive datasets; controllable/fine-grained feedback learning (Wu et al. 2023 fine-grained RLHF) and attribution work (Menick et al. 2022; Bohnet et al. 2022; Liu et al. 2023a ALCE; Min et al. 2023 FactScore).
contrasts_with: Standard fixed RAG that always retrieves a fixed number of passages (Ram et al. 2023; Lewis et al. 2020); SAIL (Luo et al. 2023, instruction-tuned with top-1 retrieved doc, no reflection) - approximated by the No-Critic ablation; Toolformer (Schick et al. 2023, learns to call tools/retrieval via special tokens but without fine-grained relevance/support critique); RLHF/PPO feedback learning (Ouyang et al. 2022; Wu et al. 2023) which needs retraining to change behavior; Recomp (Xu et al. 2023) and robustness-to-irrelevant-context (Yoran et al. 2023) which refine context differently; CoVE (self-verification). Later positioned against by Adaptive-RAG (Jeong et al. 2024) as either too simple or too complex per-query.
lineage: Group B (RAG for task solving) - the active / self-reflective / adaptive-retrieval lineage. Self-RAG is a foundational 'learned when-and-whether-to-retrieve plus self-critique' framework: it advances from fixed RAG and token-confidence-triggered active retrieval (FLARE) toward model-emitted reflection-token control, and is a key predecessor/contrast for learned-router adaptive retrieval (Adaptive-RAG), corrective/agentic RAG (CRAG, Self-Reflective RAG recipes in LangGraph/LlamaIndex), and self-critique RAG pipelines.
